advances: Preserves selected open, closed, and boundary cap masses of a genuine maximizing law under the assumed same-class repair. Arbitrary fractional boundary allocations are outside the assertion.

proof:
Fix one $\ell=a\cdot z+v\cdot x-b$. Suppose $v\ne0$. If the cut plane on $K_z$ meets its interior, the section of the boundary lies in the relative boundary of the convex section in the plane. Indeed a relative-interior point of that section has a neighborhood in the plane contained in the fiber, so any support plane there must coincide with the cut plane, which cannot support when it meets the interior. This relative boundary has zero $(d-1)$-measure, also when $d=1$ since the cut point then belongs to the fiber interior. If the plane misses the interior but meets the fiber, it supports the fiber and any regular point of the intersection has outer normal either $v/\|v\|$ or $-v/\|v\|$, according to the orientation of the support. The marked measure discards the surface-null nonregular part. Summing over the finite fibers shows the original cut has zero marked surface mass away from those two normals. Absolute continuity of the reference and disintegration give $\omega_n\{\ell=0\}=0$ for almost every such $n$. Use the hinge $\ell_+$ there.

At either parallel normal $n$, $\ell$ is constant on each face in $G_n$. For $n=v/\|v\|$ the values are $a\cdot z+\|v\|h_{K_z}(n)-b$, and for $n=-v/\|v\|$ they are $a\cdot z-\|v\|h_{K_z}(n)-b$. Choose $\delta>0$ smaller than every nonzero absolute value in the finite list, or arbitrary if the list is all zero. Then on the entire $G_n$ the closed cap at zero agrees with $\{\ell\ge-\delta\}$ and the open cap agrees with $\{\ell\ge\delta\}$. Neither shifted plane meets $G_n$. Use both hinges $(\ell+\delta)_+$ and $(\ell-\delta)_+$. If $v=0$, the same finite-gap argument works with the list $a\cdot z-b$ for every normal. The choices are Borel, since each is constant except possibly at the two specified normals for a nonvertical cap.

Combine the chosen hinges for the menu with positive weights. Compatibility forces the source to be supported on the convex hull of the compact midpoint range, by testing the convex distance to that hull. The compact source-compatible class is obtained by adding convex-order inequalities against a countable uniformly dense family of restrictions of finite continuous convex tests on the common compact physical range. The coefficients and thresholds are Borel, so the objective is Borel in the label and continuous in the coupling. To see that the maximum is Borel, for each $k$ take the supremum over a fixed countable dense subset of the compact coupling space using the first $k$ constraints strictly relaxed by $1/k$. Each relaxed set is open and contains the feasible set, so its supremum agrees with the dense-point supremum. The sets decrease, and compactness applied to nearly maximizing sequences gives the true maximum as their limit. Add equality to that maximum as two constraints and apply 9d641a80a1b194d4 to select a maximizing law. For a repair impose convex-order improvement above this selected law and the domination by $B\omega_n$, using the countable convex tests and a countable dense family of nonnegative continuous tests, respectively. The assumed repair makes this new compact feasible class nonempty, so the same selector applies. Source compatibility survives by convex-order transitivity.

The hinge maximization theorem gives equality of both cap masses at each threshold used, because the repaired boundary is null by domination at ordinary normals and by graph membership at the shifted thresholds. At parallel normals and for pure-base caps the exact graph identities recover both original cap masses. Subtraction transfers the original boundary masses. The inward selector at a regular boundary point is the usual cap indicator off the cut. On a coincident support face with outward normal $v/\|v\|$, the fiber lies in $\{\ell\le0\}$ and its inward layer is strictly outside the cap, giving the open convention. With normal $-v/\|v\|$, its inward layer lies inside, giving the closed convention. At all other normals the original cut has no mass in either midpoint law by the boundary-null contact conclusion. Thus the stated selector integrals agree in each class, and integration over labels preserves them globally.

statement:
Let $P$ be a finite set of actual integer bases with compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$ of positive $d$-volume, $d\ge1$. Let $\eta$ be the sum of the boundary surface measures marked by their outer unit normal $n$, with endpoint counting for $d=1$. Set $G_n=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times F_{K_z}(n))$, where $F_{K_z}(n)$ is the exposed face. Use conditional kernels relative to a common finite normal reference measure dominating the normal marginals in question. Assume the endpoint coupling classes in each normal and original parity are compact and given by countably many constraints on a common compact metric space of physical pair laws, Borel in the label and continuous in the candidate law. Each class fixes the two marginals and has actual midpoint support in $G_n$. Assume a Borel physical source kernel is compatible with some law in each class by convex order. Suppose every old coupling in its class has a same-class repair improving its midpoint law in convex order and satisfying $\rho_{\rm new}\le B\omega_n$, where $B<\infty$ and the Borel kernel $\omega_n$ comes from a fixed finite marked measure absolutely continuous with respect to $\eta$.

Given any finite menu of ambient affine functions $\ell_j(z,x)=a_j\cdot z+v_j\cdot x-b_j$, one can choose Borel thresholds, one or two per cap in each class, and measurably maximize their positively weighted hinge sum over source-compatible couplings. A measurable repair of the maximizing laws preserves, simultaneously, their open and closed cap masses at $\ell_j=0$ and hence also their boundary masses, conditionally in almost every normal and parity class and after integration. It preserves the inward cap selector, which uses the open convention on coincident outside support faces and the closed convention on coincident inside support faces, and either fixed convention for pure-base caps.
title: Shifted hinges preserve selected surface cap boundary atoms
